packages.title: Fuel poverty final-versus-projection QA
facts: 2026 report contains final England estimates for 2024.
The report analyses 2024 and 2025 fuel-poor groups.
It includes projections for 2025 and 2026.
Projection years must not be treated as final observations.
Fuel-poverty status is not a direct GHG measurement.

packages.title: Fuel poverty LILEE-definition QA
facts: England fuel poverty uses the LILEE indicator.
LILEE requires energy-efficiency band D or below.
LILEE also requires residual income below the poverty line after required heating costs.
Household income, energy requirements and fuel prices are inputs.
LILEE classification is not an emissions inventory value.

packages.title: Sub-regional fuel-poverty 2024 QA
facts: Sub-regional fuel-poverty data were published 14 May 2026.
The data reference year is 2024.
The measure is LILEE.
The publication applies to England.
Sub-regional household statistics must not be converted to parcel GHG values.

packages.title: Fuel-poverty household-versus-emissions QA
facts: Fuel-poverty tables describe household and dwelling characteristics.
They are socio-energy indicators rather than measured emissions.
Required heating cost is part of the LILEE concept.
Fuel prices affect the indicator.
No parcel CO2e value is published by these tables.

packages.title: Natural-capital 2025 water-correction QA
facts: ONS corrected country-level water-provisioning monetary apportionment on 19 May 2026.
The correction affected Figure 2 and detailed/summary tables.
UK-level findings were not affected.
Superseded country-level values should not be reused.
Monetary natural-capital values are not direct GHG measurements.

packages.title: Natural-capital economic-value versus GHG QA
facts: Natural-capital accounts estimate economic and social value of natural resources.
Natural assets include soil, air, water and living things.
Ecosystem-service valuation is an accounting framework.
Asset values are not tonnes of CO2e unless explicitly stated as a physical carbon flow.
Do not infer parcel emissions from monetary natural-capital values.

packages.title: Enclosed-farmland natural-capital 2026 QA
facts: ONS released enclosed-farmland natural-capital accounts on 8 July 2026.
The release covers UK enclosed farmland.
It includes economic and social values of natural resources.
Detailed and summary data tables are provided.
Farmland natural-capital values must remain distinct from parcel GHG emissions.

packages.title: Natural-capital quality/comparability QA
facts: ONS natural-capital quality guide was revised 10 July 2026.
The guide documents coverage and production methods.
It describes quality and comparability.
Method changes can affect comparability over time.
Use the stated methodology before cross-year comparisons.

packages.title: Natural-capital renewable-provisioning other-sites QA
facts: ONS renewable-electricity provisioning uses DESNZ generation data.
Country figures exclude generation classified as other sites.
Other sites are withheld from regional attribution for disclosure reasons.
Country sums therefore do not equal the UK physical-flow figure.
Do not backfill suppressed regional generation into parcels.

packages.title: Natural-capital bioenergy double-count QA
facts: ONS excludes bioenergy from renewable-electricity provisioning estimates in this account.
The exclusion avoids double counting with timber removals and agricultural biomass.
Renewable physical flows and monetary estimates are separate concepts.
Habitat assignment is methodological rather than parcel-emission measurement.
Do not reintroduce excluded bioenergy without the published method.

packages.title: Road-traffic 2025 data-quality QA
facts: DfT road-traffic website data were published 20 May 2026.
Annual estimates use about 7,000 roadside manual counts plus automatic counters and road-length data.
Regional and national traffic figures are accredited official statistics.
Road-link and small-area estimates are less robust.
Traffic volume is activity data, not direct CO2e.

packages.title: Road-traffic counted-versus-estimated QA
facts: Road-link downloads include estimation_method fields.
Counted observations are generally more accurate than estimated values.
Estimated road-link figures should be used with caution.
Local newer sources may sometimes be more accurate.
Do not represent estimated link traffic as measured parcel emissions.

packages.title: Road-traffic small-area caution QA
facts: DfT warns individual road-link estimates are not always based on current local counts.
Small-area estimates have greater uncertainty than regional totals.
Users should document limitations when publishing link-level estimates.
Local-highway data may supersede a national road-link estimate for local analysis.
A road-link estimate cannot be assigned to a land parcel without a separate spatial gate.

packages.title: Transport-environment 2024 GHG QA
facts: DfT published Transport and environment statistics: 2024 on 14 July 2026.
Domestic transport emitted 110.4 MtCO2e in 2024.
The value was about 0.2% above 2023.
Domestic transport represented 30% of UK domestic GHG emissions.
National transport totals are not parcel measurements.

packages.title: Transport GHG-versus-air-pollutant QA
facts: The DfT release reports both GHG and air pollutants.
Domestic transport contributed 29% of domestic NOx in 2024.
It contributed 26% of domestic PM2.5 and 22% of PM10.
NOx and particulate shares must not be expressed as CO2e.
Pollutant families require separate units and inventories.

packages.title: Transport-environment table-coverage QA
facts: ENV tables cover fuel consumption, GHG, pollutants and journey emissions.
Coverage periods differ by table according to source availability.
Each table name states its period coverage.
Petroleum mode detail is sourced via ECUK table C8 rather than ENV0101 for recent breakdowns.
Cross-table comparisons must preserve year and metric coverage.

packages.title: NAEI GHG 2026 vintage QA
facts: NAEI GHG data page was updated 9 June 2026.
The 2026 UK GHG Inventory covers 1990 to 2024.
Publication year and inventory data year are different fields.
Future next-publication dates must not be treated as released data.
Inventory totals remain distinct from parcel measurements.

packages.title: NAEI point/grid vintage QA
facts: NAEI lists point-source and gridded datasets separately.
Some listed point-source and gridded products still reference 2023 data vintages.
A 2026 page update does not make every underlying dataset 2026 data.
Dataset vintage must be read from the product title.
Gridded or point-source data require a separate geometry binding step for parcel use.

packages.title: NAEI air-pollutant/GHG separation QA
facts: NAEI provides separate air-pollutant and greenhouse-gas inventories.
Air pollutants include NOx, PM, SO2, ammonia and NMVOC.
GHG inventory covers direct greenhouse gases under the Paris Agreement.
Air pollutant mass must not be converted to CO2e without an explicit valid method.
The two inventory families have different reporting frameworks.

packages.title: NAEI projection-versus-observation QA
facts: NAEI air-quality projections use activity and emission-factor assumptions.
Projected emissions are model outputs for future years.
Projection methodology follows inventory-guidebook principles.
Projected emissions are not observed historical emissions.
Do not use projections as parcel measurements.

packages.title: NAEI devolved-IAS boundary QA
facts: Devolved air-pollutant inventories use UK territorial coverage rules.
International aviation and shipping estimates are shown separately because they are excluded from national inventory data under UNECE protocols.
Offshore oil and gas may be reported as unallocated rather than assigned to a country.
Country totals must preserve these exclusions.
Do not force unallocated or IAS emissions into parcel records.

packages.title: EA Pollution Inventory partial-year QA
facts: EA Pollution Inventory reporting covers regulated industrial releases and transfers.
Newly operating sites report the period they were operational.
Measured emissions use what was actually recorded for that period.
Calculated emissions must be adjusted to the operating period.
Partial-year values must not be silently annualised.
